messages:
Ellen (AE): BlueNova asking for Private deployment POC. They require strict IP-based allowlists. Can we give a crisp PrivateLink vs peering recommendation, a firewall snippet their netops can paste, and a 3-week POC cost ETA for ~12k req/day (~120GB)?

Hari (NetEng): Short: PrivateLink = fastest (no routing changes, interface endpoints per AZ). Peering/TGW = preserves client source IP and lets customer egress via static EIP (best for IP allowlists and audits). If the customer mandates IP-only allowlists long term, plan for peering + NAT with static EIPs.

Zoe (Solutions): Recommended flow: try PrivateLink first to validate in 1-2 business days; if they can't accept ephemeral ENI IPs, move to peering/TGW which takes 3-7 days depending on approvals.

Omar (Sec): We support mutual TLS and cert rotation for POCs. We can provide a short-lived ENI IP snapshot for auditors during the validation window but note it's brittle. For auditable, long-term allowlisting, peering with customer-controlled EIPs is the clean path.

Hari (NetEng): Firewall snippet they can paste (customer side):
```
# Minimal outbound rules for PrivateLink POC
allow tcp 443 from <app-subnet-cidr> to <vpce-enis-or-sg>   # HTTPS to Redwood via interface endpoints
allow udp 53 from <app-subnet-cidr> to <dns-resolver>     # DNS
allow udp 123 from <app-subnet-cidr> to 0.0.0.0/0         # NTP
# If peering + static EIP: allow tcp 443 to <static-egress-eip>
```
Prefer SGs on the endpoint rather than hard-coding many IPs.

Zoe (Solutions): Ballpark 3-week POC cost (PrivateLink): AWS data processing ~ $0.01-$0.03/GB => ~ $1.20-$3.60 for 120GB; endpoint hours small (region/AZ dependent). Redwood POC support/hand-holding typically $1k-$3k for networking-heavy trials. Add NAT/EIP costs if they choose peering.

WorkflowBot: Created ticket POC-9001 for BlueNova connectivity handoff; assigned to Hari. Validation window Thu 09:30-10:00.

Ellen (AE): I'll send this as a one-pager to BlueNova, attach the snippet and the POC budget range, and propose PrivateLink first with peering as fallback. Thanks all :thumbsup:
